name: Apixaban
summary: A direct oral anticoagulant used for stroke prevention and venous thromboembolism treatment or prophylaxis.
good: Patients who need an oral anticoagulant with predictable dosing and no INR routine.
bad: Major interaction burden or scenarios where specific reversal/monitoring logic has not been reviewed.
clinicalPearls: No routine INR monitoring is needed, but missed doses matter because the anticoagulant effect is shorter-lived than warfarin.
mechanism: Directly inhibits factor Xa, interrupting thrombin generation in the coagulation cascade.
indications: Atrial fibrillation stroke prevention, DVT/PE treatment, and extended VTE prevention.
interactionNotes: Strong CYP3A4 and P-gp modifiers can increase or decrease exposure.

warnings: Bleeding risk, renal/hepatic impairment, and adherence are the major issues.
